name: Sunday Morning Wrestling Show

date.source: The fed's own multi-part broadcast posting, billed the first-ever edition of the Sunday Morning Wrestling Show.

evidence.source: The fed's own multi-part broadcast posting, now served in full.
evidence.note: The first Sunday Morning Wrestling Show of the fed's 1999 return, from the Alcair Dal Stadium.

matches.note: The champion retained after his manager distracted the referee.
The champion retained, reversing a top-rope piledriver into a pinning combination after the challenger's own ally interfered against him.

appearances.source: Announced every decision on the fed's own 25 April 1999 broadcast.

no_appearances_reason: The broadcast also carried a jobber squashing, a burrito-stipulation match, a hardcore yak match, a cage match and a pure wrestling match, plus interview and vignette segments; only the two title matches above are named here.
notes: The first Sunday Morning Wrestling Show of the fed's 1999 return, establishing that both the Galactic and Orange Grove Texas titles carried unbroken across the fed's five-month hiatus.

name: Chucklemasters

date.source: The fed's own multi-part broadcast posting.

evidence.source: The fed's own multi-part broadcast posting, now served in full.
evidence.note: Crowned the fed's first-ever World Tag Teem Champions after a contested tournament finish.

matches.stipulation: Deciding match for the vacant LOL World Tag Teem title
matches.note: Set up after an earlier elimination tournament for the previously vacant title ended in controversy: the team believed eliminated made off with the belts by disguise before this deciding match settled the championship.

appearances.source: Announced every decision on the fed's own 3 June 1999 broadcast.

no_appearances_reason: The broadcast's own tag team elimination tournament involved several further teams before the deciding match above; only the two teams who contested the deciding fall are named here.
notes: Crowned the Real American Zeroes the fed's first-ever World Tag Teem Champions, after an elimination tournament whose contested finish was settled by a further deciding match on the same broadcast.

name: Sunday Morning Wrestling Show

date.source: The fed's own multi-part broadcast posting, from the Cuban National Ballet Theatre in Havana.

evidence.source: The fed's own multi-part broadcast posting, now served in full.
evidence.note: The Orange Grove Texas title changed hands; the Galactic title was retained by disqualification.

matches.note: The champion retained after a rival wrestler struck him with a pizza at ringside, an act the challenger himself reported to the referee rather than capitalise on.
The title changed hands; the broadcast's own announce team called the finish live as a new champion was crowned.

appearances.source: Announced every decision on the fed's own 6 June 1999 broadcast.

no_appearances_reason: The broadcast also carried a statue-judging contest, a comedy vignette and interview segments; only the two title matches above are named here.
notes: The only broadcast in the surviving 1999 record on which the Orange Grove Texas title changed hands.

name: Laugh Attack

date.source: The fed's own multi-part broadcast posting, from the deck of a fictional aircraft carrier off the Cuban coast.

evidence.source: The fed's own multi-part broadcast posting, now served in full.
evidence.note: The World Tag Teem title changed hands eleven days after it was first awarded.

matches.note: The title changed hands to a pairing formed for this match alone, aided by interference from a third wrestler against the champions; the partnership broke up days later.

appearances.source: Announced every decision on the fed's own 14 June 1999 broadcast.

no_appearances_reason: The broadcast also carried a six-man tag match, a lightsaber-stipulation match and a statue-judging contest; only the title match above is named here.
notes: Van Halent became the only wrestler in the fed's own record to hold both the Galactic and World Tag Teem titles at once; the pairing that won the belts here broke up within days.

name: Chucklemasters

date.source: The fed's own broadcast posting, taped from the officer's mess of the same fictional aircraft carrier.

evidence.source: The fed's own broadcast posting, now served in full.
evidence.note: The fed's on-screen Chancellor held up the World Tag Teem title after the reigning champions' partnership broke up.

appearances.source: Announced the World Tag Teem title held up on the fed's own 17 June 1999 broadcast, and set a rematch for 28 June 1999.
Announced every decision on the fed's own 17 June 1999 broadcast.

no_appearances_reason: The broadcast also carried an open-contract angle and jobber squashings; only the title-holdup angle above is named here.
notes: The Chancellor of the LOL held the World Tag Teem title up rather than let it be defended by champions whose own partnership had broken up, and announced a rematch for 28 June 1999 -- a date the surviving record does not reach before the promotion's second and final closure five days later.
